subject: Acme Analytics: intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes impacting ingestion pipelines
messages:
From: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-ops@acmeanalytics.com, thomas.lee@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden increase in timeouts — p99 spikes starting 11/27

Connor,

We're seeing a sharp increase in failing ingestion jobs overnight — p95 looks slightly up but p99 is spiking to 8–10s, which is breaching our downstream timeouts and causing retries and duplicates. This started around 2026-11-27 22:00 PST and has continued in bursts.

Symptoms:
- Ingestion HTTP 504 / gateway timeouts at our side for calls to your hosted endpoint.
- Request IDs: 7f3b2a, 7f3b2b, 7f3b8c (sample attached).
- Our internal retry logic showed many back-to-back requests for the same payload; we've attached a short CSV of p99 timeseries and error snippets.

Can you confirm whether there were any infra changes or known regressions in the hosted API around that time? Our SLOs are firm and this is causing downstream failures — we need an update and an ETA on a fix.

Thanks,
Elaine
Principal SRE, Acme Analytics
Acme Analytics | elaine.wu@acmeanalytics.com

Attachments: p99_sample_timeseries.csv, acme_error_snippet.txt

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden increase in timeouts — p99 spikes starting 11/27

Hi Elaine — thanks for the report and the artifacts. I'm escalating this internally now and looping in our SRE and PM.

Immediate ask for us to triage faster:
1) Could you share client-side SDK version and your effective request timeout/ retry settings (attached snippet helps).
2) If you can, temporarily increase your client timeout to 12s and disable aggressive retries for a small cohort — that will help us disambiguate client vs server.

We'll dig into p95/p99 trends and trace samples on our side. I know the timing is sensitive — we'll aim to provide a preliminary root cause within 2 hours.

Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0197

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Acme Analytics / ACME-4793 — investigation (internal)

Team — forwarding Acme's report. Key points:
- Customer reports intermittent p99 spikes up to ~8–10s starting 11/27 22:00 PST, impacting ingestion pipelines.
- They attached request ids and a timeseries CSV.
- They observe many back-to-back retries from their side.

Action items:
- Dylan: can you pull raw traces for Acme's org and the gateway around 2026-11-27 21:45–23:30 PST? Focus on token generation times vs gateway queuing.
- Hannah: customer is sensitive to SLO breaches; help coordinate comms and prepare a short customer-facing summary w/ mitigation steps.
- Markus: raising to you because this looks like an escalation that may need exec attention if we confirm multi-region impact.

Please reply with status and ETA. I'll keep Acme updated that we're investigating and will escalate if we see platform-side regressions.

Connor

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Analytics / ACME-4793 — investigation (internal)

Quick update from tracing and sampling: 
- I pulled gateway traces for the timestamp window Connor requested. Overall host-side model token generation mostly stable; median generation latency is normal.
- The majority of gateway p99 events correlate with a pattern: repeated identical requests from the same client IP within short windows (~500–1200ms). Those windows line up with the customer's retry loop.
- We see that the gateway is receiving 2–6 near-duplicate requests for the same logical idempotency key, which causes queueing and inflates p99 measurements for the gateway endpoint because retries get enqueued behind in-flight requests.

Excerpt (sanitized) from trace_samples.json: 
{"request_id":"7f3b2a","events":[{"phase":"ingress","t":0},{"phase":"gateway_queue","t":46},{"phase":"model_call","t":1800}],"observed_duplicates":3}

Preliminary hypothesis: client-side timeouts + immediate retries are generating a retry-storm pattern that inflates our observed p95/p99 on the gateway. In some bursts, the increased concurrency pushes a small fraction of requests into higher queues, causing downstream 504s at the customer's ingestion service.

Recommended mitigation steps (short term):
1) Advise customer to increase client timeout to 12s and add exponential backoff on retries (jitter).
2) Advise enabling idempotency keys or ensure their SDK sets idempotency when reissuing.
3) On our side, we can add more aggressive deduplication on identical idempotency keys in the gateway to limit redundant downstream model calls — we'll scope work.

I'll attach the sampled traces (trace_samples.json) and a short analysis. I'll keep digging for any server-side anomalies but nothing obvious yet.

-Dylan
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: trace_samples.json

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Wu <elaine.wu@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 12:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden increase in timeouts — p99 spikes starting 11/27

Elaine — thanks for your patience. Summary of our preliminary findings: 
- We do not see a platform-wide kernel or model regression at the timestamps you provided. Median server-side latencies are in range.
- However, traces show a pattern of many near-duplicate requests from your SDK within short windows. Those retries are increasing gateway queueing and artificially inflating our p99 measurements for your organization. The duplicates also contribute to downstream burstiness that's likely triggering your ingestion timeouts.

Immediate suggestions we recommend you try now (small test):
- Temporarily increase request timeout in your SDK to 12s.
- Disable immediate retry, enable exponential backoff with jitter (initial backoff 250ms).
- If possible, turn on idempotency keys (SDK v2.1.4+ sets these by default).

If you want, our SRE (Dylan) can be on a quick call to observe traces while you run the test. We also have a KB article: https://docs.redwood.com/kb/client-retry-attribution that explains this pattern and includes an SDK checklist.

We'll continue to monitor on our side and scope a gateway dedup mitigation to reduce blast radius for identical idempotent retries.

Best,
Connor

Connor / Hannah — thanks for the fast triage and the clear customer-facing summary. Two asks: 
1) Please prepare a short postmortem (1–2 pages) describing the root cause, mitigations we applied/recommended, and timelines to a permanent fix (gateway dedupe, or server-side idempotency enforcement). Include customer impact metrics (p95/p99, error rate, requests duplicated).
2) Assess customer relief (one-time credit / SLA exception). Finance/sales will want a recommended credit amount tied to impact.

Priority: high. If you need executive help with the customer call, let me know and I'll join.

-Markus
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
notes: Customer initially escalated p99 spikes; internal tracing pointed to client-side retry storms inflating gateway p99; internal plan: triage, customer mitigation guidance, scope gateway dedup and customer relief.
